planName: Order Service Java 25 and Spring Boot 4 Modernization

entries.taskSummary: Snapshotted 'app/Java - Spring Boot/Order Service' to an isolated temp folder and built the frozen baseline exclusively from that snapshot, independent of any in-flight migration/upgrade tasks. Ran the full backend suite (mvn test) from the snapshot: BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run 20 / Failures 0 / Errors 0 / Skipped 0 across OrderRepositoryTest, OrderServiceTest, OrderServiceUnitTest, and OrderControllerTest. Ran the frontend suite/build from the snapshot: npm test (node --test) 4/4 passed; npm run build succeeded (36 modules transformed). Authored src/test/test-cases/test-cases.md documenting the Order API contract, validation rules, H2 persistence assumptions, CORS/web config, the full backend test inventory, the frontend view-logic contract, and a frozen infra-decision table selecting MOCKED external dependencies for every dependency (H2 kept embedded/in-process; no Azure resource, credential, or connection referenced anywhere, per the no-provisioned-Azure-environment constraint). Added testdata/seeded-orders.json, testdata/sample-requests.json, and testdata/frontend-orders-fixture.json as frozen fixtures. Copied only these frozen artifacts back into the live workspace under src/test/test-cases/ (production source untouched) and committed them on the current branch. The folder is now FROZEN.
risks: The frozen baseline was captured against the pre-upgrade Java 8 / Spring Boot 2.7.18 source snapshot; if the Java 25 / Spring Boot 4 upgrade (task 001) changes observable behavior beyond the frozen contract (e.g. validation error format, enum bind error status), Phase 3 PostMigrationIT tests will surface it as a regression requiring an explicit unfreeze/re-freeze cycle rather than a silent fix.

No provisioned Azure environment exists for this plan; the infra-decision table freezes every external dependency to a MOCKED/embedded strategy (H2 in-memory), so this baseline cannot detect regressions specific to a real Azure-hosted database or service.
followUps: When Phase 3 (integrationTest) runs, verify all *PostMigrationIT scenarios against the frozen test-cases.md using only mocked/embedded substitutes, with no Azure credentials required.

If a future plan provisions real Azure resources, re-run setupBaseline's re-freeze cycle to update the infra-decision table from MOCKED to a live-resource strategy before relying on it for verification.

entries.taskSummary: Materialized the FROZEN app/Java - Spring Boot/Order Service/src/test/test-cases/test-cases.md spec as *PostMigrationIT tests against the migrated Java 25 / Spring Boot 4.1.1 implementation and executed them with mocked/embedded dependencies only (no Azure credentials, resources, or connections used or required). Added 3 append-only JUnit 5 IT classes (23 methods): OrderPersistencePostMigrationIT (5, @DataJpaTest, mirrors OrderRepositoryTest), OrderServicePostMigrationIT (7, @SpringBootTest with real repository/H2, mirrors OrderServiceUnitTest+OrderServiceTest, asserts via persisted DB state), OrderApiPostMigrationIT (11, full @SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)+TestRestTemplate, mirrors all 9 OrderControllerTest scenarios plus seeded-row presence and a CORS preflight check). Added maven-failsafe-plugin so *PostMigrationIT classes run via `mvn verify` distinct from the existing Surefire *Test suite; added a test-scoped spring-boot-starter-restclient dependency required for TestRestTemplate under Spring Boot 4's modularized test infrastructure. `mvn clean verify` (JDK 26.0.2, the only non-EOL JDK available on this host) -> BUILD SUCCESS: Surefire 20/20 pre-existing unit tests unchanged and passing, Failsafe 23/23 new *PostMigrationIT tests passing (43/43 backend tests total, non-zero execution evidence, no compile-only/zero-test runs). Frontend: `npm install` -> 0 vulnerabilities; `npm test` -> 4/4 passed (unchanged orderView.js scenarios); `npm run build` (vite 8.2.2) -> succeeded, 20 modules transformed (vs 36 at baseline capture -- an internal Vite 8 bundling optimization detail, not an output-contract change). All 24 frozen scenarios (20 backend + 4 frontend) re-proven passing; zero behavior regressions found. Documented adaptation-only differences: (1) TestRestTemplate relocated to org.springframework.boot.resttestclient and now needs @AutoConfigureTestRestTemplate + spring-boot-starter-restclient; (2) Spring Boot 4 defaults to Jackson 3.x under tools.jackson.* (test-code import change only, no wire-contract change); (3) discovered and worked around (not a regression, pre-existing latent behavior) a named in-memory H2 database (jdbc:h2:mem:orders;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1) accumulating DataSeeder rows when multiple full @SpringBootTest context configurations boot in the same test JVM -- tests were designed with dedicated per-test customer names to stay deterministic; production single-startup behavior is unaffected.
risks: This verification is mock-only (embedded H2, no live Azure resource); it cannot detect regressions specific to a real Azure-hosted database, network latency, or managed-service-specific behavior, consistent with the frozen infra-decision table since no Azure environment is provisioned for this plan.

Verification ran on JDK 26.0.2 rather than the JDK 25.0.2 distribution used in task 001, because JDK 25.0.2 was not installed on this host at verification time; both are Java-25-language-level compatible for this project (source/target 25) and all tests passed, but a future run should confirm on the exact JDK 25.0.2 distribution if strict parity is required.

A pre-existing (non-migration) fragility in the app's named in-memory H2 database configuration causes DataSeeder to reseed when multiple full @SpringBootTest context configurations share the same test JVM; not a production-impacting issue but worth a future code-level fix (e.g. a per-test-class unique H2 database name or @DirtiesContext) if more full-context IT suites are added later.
followUps: If a future plan provisions real Azure resources, re-run setupBaseline's re-freeze cycle and add corresponding *PostMigrationIT coverage against the live resource before removing the MOCKED-only constraint.

Consider isolating the H2 in-memory database name per full-context test class (or adding @DirtiesContext) to remove the latent DataSeeder double-seeding fragility discovered during this verification, independent of any further migration work.
